2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this writ petition are as follows:
3. The land of respondent No.1 was acquired for the purpose of construction of Railway Line under a Notification.
The SLAO passed an award under Section 23 of Land Acquisition Act, 2013.

The claimant filed reference application under Section 64(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) before the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Koppal, and it was numbered as LAC No.133/2020.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Koppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Reference Court allowed the LAC in part and the market value of the acquired land was enhanced at the rate of Rs.800/- per sq.ft. with all statutory benefits.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3368 HC-KAR 4.
The petitioner aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Reference Court, preferred an appeal before this Court in MFA No.103224/2023.
The Division Bench of this Court granted an interim order of stay subject to deposit of 50% of the award amount.
The petitioner did not deposit 50% of the award amount as ordered by the Division Bench of this Court.
5. It is contended that the petitioner filed an application for modification of the interim order granted by this Court.
It is contended that respondent No.1 filed an execution petition before the learned V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Hubballi, and the petitioner filed a memo for depositing Rs.7,50,000/-.

entities.text: V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Hubballi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is contended that the Executing Court has issued arrest warrant against the officers of the petittioner's department.
Hence, this writ petition.

6. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent Nos.2 and 3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has filed an application for modification of the interim NC: 2026:KHC-D:3368 HC-KAR order passed in the appeal before the Division Bench and the said application is pending.
The Executing Court has issued arrest warrant against the officers of the petitioner's department.
Hence, on this ground prays to allow the writ petition.

8. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
9.
It is an undisputed fact that the land of respondent No.1 was acquired for the purpose of construction of Railway Line.
The SLAO has passed an award.
Respondent No.1 filed a reference application under Section 64(1) of the Act in LAC No.133/2020.
The Reference Court allowed the reference application and enhanced the market value at the rate of Rs.800/- per sq.ft with all statutory benefits.
10. The petitioner aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Reference Court preferred MFA No.103224/2023 before this Court.

The Division Bench of this Court granted an interim order on 11.11.2025 staying the execution and operation of the judgment and award in LAC No.133/2020 subject to the petitioner depositing 50% of the award amount along with the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3368 HC-KAR interest and other statutory benefits before the reference Court.
Pursuant to the interim order, the petitioner has partly deposited the award amount but not 50% of the award amount.

Respondent No.1 filed an Execution Petition No.5233/2025 wherein the Executing Court has issued attachment warrant of moveable properties and not an arrest warrant against the officers of the petitioner.
The petitioner is under a wrong impression that an arrest warrant is issued against the officers of the petitioner.

The Executing Court has issued an attachment of moveable properties of the petitioner, as the petitioner has not complied with the interim order passed by the Division Bench of this Court in the aforesaid MFA.

The Executing Court has rightly passed the impugned order at Annexure-A.
11.
Hence, I do not find any ground to entertain the writ petition.
Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
Pending applications, if any, stands disposed off.

Sd/-
 (ASHOK S. KINAGI)
